question: to the Commission Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE) Subject:

According to Frontex data, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency has around 3 400 deployed officers performing tasks supporting Member States’ authorities in the area of immigration and border protection. One of the tasks of these officers – in support of the border police –is to interview newly arrived illegal immigrants. During such interviews, immigrants may provide information, for example, on places through which they have transited or on the criminal networks that have provided them with transport. With the regulation on screening due to come into force1, these interviews may play a more significant role in ensuring the effectiveness of any returns and in the fight against criminal networks. In this regard, in statements to Euractiv2, the Agency itself has indicated that it has serious problems sharing this data with the police, as the EDPS has established that this would be in breach of the Regulation governing its operation. 1.
Is the Commission aware of this problem?
Is an urgent amendment of the Frontex Regulation being prepared to address these limitations in the flow of key information?
Are the relevant Commission services in contact with the national authorities and Interpol to assess any initiatives that would render the fight against illegal immigration effective?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1356 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 introducing the screening of third-country nationals at the external borders. https://www.euractiv.com/news/frontex-blocked-from-sharing-data-on-human-traffickers/.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.6.2026) The European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) performs its operational activities, including debriefing interviews with migrants, under the command and control of the Member States concerned. In this respect, Frontex cannot be considered precluded from sharing data obtained from these interviews with the relevant national authorities. Moreover, when these interviews produce data potentially relevant for the fight against cross-border crime, Article 90 of Regulation (EU) 2019/18961 explicitly mandates Frontex to share this operational personal data with the relevant national law enforcement authorities. The Commission is not aware of any recommendations or opinions of the European Data Protection Supervisor that would indicate that sharing operational personal data with national police authorities would be in breach of this Regulation, as long as the applicable data protection framework is respected. The Commission intends to propose a revision of Regulation (EU) 2019/1896 in 2026. The preparatory work is ongoing, including as regards the contributions that Frontex can provide to the Member States and relevant EU agencies in the fight against cross-border crime, including with regard to information exchange. To counter migrant smuggling, the Commission engages regularly with the national authorities, both through European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling2 set up by the EU Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol) and via the EU Policy Cycle and the Operational Action Plan3 Migrant Smuggling where Member States, EU Agencies, partners and international organisations, such as the International Criminal Police Organisation (Interpol), regularly engage in targeted operational activities.
1 Regulation (EU) 2019/1896 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 November 2019 on the

European Border and Coast Guard and repealing Regulations (EU) No 1052/2013 and (EU) 2016/1624, OJ L 295, p. 1. 2 https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom/news/grip-migrant-smuggling-tightens-newdepartment-europol-to-step-fight. From March 2026, the activities of the European Migrant Smuggling Centre were taken over by the European Centre Against Migrant Smuggling (ECAMS; https://www.europol.europa.eu/about-europol/european-centre-against-migrant-smuggling-ecams) and the European Serious and Organised Crime Centre (ESOCC; https://www.europol.europa.eu/abouteuropol/european-serious-and-organised-crime-centre-esocc). 3 https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/internal-security/law-enforcement-cooperation/empact-fightingcrime-together_en.
